title: Vendor security assessment questionnaire template — inference vendors
content:
Purpose:
This is a working template for initial vendor security assessments specifically tailored for providers of inference/runtime, model hosting, and related services. Use this questionnaire for both hosted and private deployment evaluations. The goal is to quickly identify high-risk areas that require contract controls (DPA addenda, SOC reports, KMS requirements), and produce a concise risk summary for Legal/Procurement and Product Security.

How to use:
- Send as an initial questionnaire to vendor security contact. Mark answers as: Yes / No / Partial / N/A + free text.
- Ask for evidence links (attestations, SOC/ISO/PCI reports, pen test reports, architecture diagrams).
- If vendor answers "Partial" or "No", insert required mitigations for contract scope (e.g., encryption at rest, dedicated tenancy, log retention).
- For vendors supporting private deployments, include deployment-specific items under section 3.

Scoring guidance (internal):
- Green: no contractual changes expected; documented evidence provided.
- Yellow: remediation plan + timeline required; contract controls likely.
- Red: block or require dedicated engineering/legal review.

SECTION 1 — ORGANIZATION & COMPLIANCE
1.1 Company legal entity and primary contact (name, role, security contact email).
1.2 Do you have a current SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate? If yes, provide latest report date and scope.
1.3 Do you undergo annual third-party penetration tests? Provide summary date and remediation status.
1.4 Do you have a dedicated security team and a named CISO or security lead? Provide SLAs for incident response.
Notes: Evidence requested: PDF reports, pen-test executive summary, contact for third-party attestations.

SECTION 2 — DATA PROTECTION & PROCESSING
2.1 Describe the categories of data your service processes when customers run inference (e.g., raw prompt text, embeddings, telemetry).
2.2 Can customers restrict retention of prompts, outputs, and telemetry? Describe retention defaults and maximum retention.
2.3 Do you provide a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) that includes: data processing details, subprocessors list, breach notification timelines, and deletion/return clauses? Attach current DPA.
2.4 How is customer data isolated? Multi-tenant logical separation described? Options for dedicated tenancy?
2.5 Are there any use or training rights asserted over customer data (e.g., training models on customer prompts)? If yes, describe opt-out or contract controls.
2.6 Where is customer data stored (regions, cloud provider)? Can we require data residency?

SECTION 3 — PRIVATE DEPLOYMENTS & ON-PREMISE OPTIONS
3.1 Do you support VPC-hosted control plane + customer-managed compute (private deployment)? Document architecture and components that remain under vendor control.
3.2 For on-prem or air-gapped deployments, what artifacts are required (images, installers, helm charts)? Is remote support available? If so, how is access provided and logged?
3.3 Can we integrate with our KMS/HSM for key management? Provide supported KMS vendors and limitations.
3.4 Describe network requirements and recommended firewall rules for private deployments.
3.5 What data leaves the customer environment (telemetry, health checks)? Can telemetry be disabled?
Notes: For private deployments, require: no vendor training rights, ability to use customer KMS, clear offline upgrade process, and audit log export.

SECTION 4 — CRYPTOGRAPHY & KEY MANAGEMENT
4.1 Are data at rest encrypted by default? Provide algorithms and key management approach.
4.2 Is data in transit encrypted (TLS versions, certificate management)?
4.3 Can customers provide their own encryption keys? Describe key rotation and access controls.
4.4 Are dev/test environments separated from production (and encrypted)?

SECTION 5 — ACCESS CONTROL & IDENTITY
5.1 Describe identity model for operators and support engineers. Do you support SSO (SAML/OIDC)?
5.2 Role-based access controls (RBAC) — provide default roles and granularity (project, model, route).
5.3 Do you perform background checks on personnel with access to customer data?
5.4 How are privileged operations (e.g., data deletion, key access) audited and authorized?

SECTION 6 — INFRASTRUCTURE & OPERATIONS
6.1 Which cloud providers, regions, and instance types do you use for hosted inference? Provide multi-region & failover approach.
6.2 Describe your autoscaling and capacity controls — how do you prevent noisy neighbor impacts?
6.3 How is model artifact integrity verified? Do you provide signed model bundles or checksums?
6.4 How do you manage secrets (service tokens, credentials) in your runtime?
6.5 What backup/restore processes exist for model artifacts and configuration? Recovery RTO/RPO targets?

SECTION 7 — MONITORING, LOGGING & AUDITABILITY
7.1 What telemetry do you collect by default (latency, errors, prompt lengths, token counts)? Is payload-level logging enabled?
7.2 Can we export audit logs (authentication, config changes, admin actions) to our SIEM? List formats and delivery mechanisms (S3, syslog, API).
7.3 How long are logs retained? Provide options for retention and archival.
7.4 Do you support traceability from API request to underlying compute instance / model version?

SECTION 8 — INCIDENT RESPONSE & SECURITY OPERATIONS
8.1 Describe your incident response process and SLAs for notification to customers in case of a confirmed data breach.
8.2 Provide timeline expectations for investigation updates and root cause analysis delivery.
8.3 Do you offer a customer-facing incident portal or post-incident report template?
8.4 Have you experienced a security incident involving customer data in the last 36 months? If yes, provide high-level summary and remediation.

SECTION 9 — SUPPLY CHAIN & THIRD PARTIES
9.1 Do you use third-party subprocessors (e.g., managed databases, observability providers)? Provide a current list and change notification process.
9.2 How do you vet subprocessors (security questionnaires, attestations, contract language)?
9.3 Are there any single points of failure in your supplier chain (e.g., proprietary model provider)?

SECTION 10 — PENETRATION TESTING & VULNERABILITY MANAGEMENT
10.1 Frequency of vulnerability scanning and patching cadence for runtime infrastructure.
10.2 Do you run regular application/infra pentests? Is remediation tracked in a public CVE/ticket summary?
10.3 How do you notify customers of critical CVEs that may affect inference workloads or underlying libs (e.g., CUDA, container runtime)?

SECTION 11 — CONTRACT / LEGAL CONTROLS (FOR LEGAL TEAM TO REVIEW)
11.1 Minimum DPA clauses we require: data processing details, subprocessors, breach notification 72 hours, deletion rights within X days, no training rights without opt-in, right to audit.
11.2 For Dedicated/Private deployments: require KMS integration, no vendor access without explicit customer approval, support SLA and availability credits.
11.3 Insurance: list cyber liability coverage and limits.

Appendix A — Example minimum answers (internal guidance)
- SOC2 Type II: Preferred. If not available, require compensating controls and larger contractual audit rights.
- Training rights: Deny. Customer data must not be used to improve or train vendor models for other customers.
- Telemetry: Must be opt-out for payload-level logs in private deployments.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add quick checkbox view for Procurement intake form.
- Confirm exact DPA wording for "broad use" vs "analysis only" of prompts (Legal to draft).
- Decide contract response timeline expectations for vendors without SOC2.

Deliverables from vendor when questionnaire returned:
- Completed questionnaire (with date and responder name).
- Copies of attestation reports (SOC2 / ISO) or self-assessment if not available.
- Architecture diagram for hosted and private deployment options.
- Subprocessor list and data flow diagram.

Sign-off: Security reviewer, Legal reviewer, Product owner (for functional acceptance).

Document history:
- 2024-08-14: initial draft by Maya Ortiz
- 2024-11-02: added private deployment section (Evan Brooks)
- 2025-03-10: clarifications on telemetry + DPA bullets (Priya Natarajan)

End of template.
